revenue_by_merchant.sql:
SELECT m.merchant_name,
       SUM(t.amount) as total_revenue,
       COUNT(*) as txn_count
FROM fact_transactions t, dim_merchant m
WHERE t.merchant_id = m.merchant_id
AND t.transaction_date > '2024-01-01'
GROUP BY m.merchant_name
ORDER BY total_revenue
LIMIT 10;

issues.title: Missing filter for completed transactions
issues.problem: The query does not filter transactions by status 'COMPLETED' to calculate revenue.
issues.fix: Add AND t.status = 'COMPLETED' to the WHERE clause.

issues.title: Implicit join syntax
issues.problem: Using implicit join syntax can lead to less readable and potentially harder to maintain code.
issues.fix: Replace the comma-separated tables in the FROM clause with an explicit JOIN.

issues.title: Lack of comments
issues.problem: The query lacks comments explaining the logic, which can make it harder for others to understand.
issues.fix: Add comments to explain the purpose of the query and its logic.

review.corrected_sql: SELECT m.merchant_name, SUM(t.amount) as total_revenue, COUNT(*) as txn_count FROM fact_transactions t JOIN dim_merchant m ON t.merchant_id = m.merchant_id WHERE t.transaction_date > '2024-01-01' AND t.status = 'COMPLETED' GROUP BY m.merchant_name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 10;
review.summary: The query had a critical correctness issue by not filtering for completed transactions. It also used an implicit join and lacked comments, affecting readability.

customer_spend.sql:
SELECT c.customer_name, c.email, c.tier,
       SUM(t.amount) as lifetime_value,
       COUNT(t.transaction_id) as total_orders
FROM dim_customer c
LEFT JOIN fact_transactions t ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id
WHERE t.status = 'COMPLETED'
GROUP BY c.customer_name, c.email
HAVING SUM(t.amount) > 1000
ORDER BY lifetime_value DESC;

issues.title: Incorrect SUM calculation
issues.problem: The SUM calculation includes all transactions, not just those with status 'COMPLETED'.
issues.fix: SUM(CASE WHEN t.status = 'COMPLETED' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END) as lifetime_value

issues.title: Missing filter for 'COMPLETED' transactions
issues.problem: The WHERE clause should be in the JOIN condition to ensure all customers are included, even those without completed transactions.
issues.fix: LEFT JOIN fact_transactions t ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id AND t.status = 'COMPLETED'

issues.title: Lack of comments
issues.problem: The query lacks comments explaining the logic and calculations.
issues.fix: Add comments to explain the purpose of each part of the query.

review.corrected_sql:
SELECT c.customer_name, c.email, c.tier,
       SUM(CASE WHEN t.status = 'COMPLETED' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END) as lifetime_value,
       COUNT(t.transaction_id) as total_orders
FROM dim_customer c
LEFT JOIN fact_transactions t ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id AND t.status = 'COMPLETED'
GROUP BY c.customer_name, c.email
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN t.status = 'COMPLETED' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END) > 1000
ORDER BY lifetime_value DESC;
review.summary: The query had issues with the calculation of lifetime value and missing filters. Readability was also lacking due to the absence of comments.

daily_failure_rate.sql:
SELECT transaction_date,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fact_transactions f2
        WHERE f2.status = 'FAILED'
        AND f2.transaction_date = t.transaction_date) as failed_count,
       COUNT(*) as total_count,
       failed_count / total_count * 100 as failure_rate
FROM fact_transactions t
GROUP BY transaction_date
ORDER BY transaction_date;

issues.title: Incorrect calculation of failure rate
issues.problem: The failure rate is being calculated incorrectly by dividing failed_count by total_count per day, instead of using the total number of transactions.

issues.title: Correlated subquery
issues.line: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fact_transactions f2 WHERE f2.status = 'FAILED' AND f2.transaction_date = t.transaction_date
issues.problem: The correlated subquery can be inefficient as it runs for each row in the outer query.
issues.fix: Use a JOIN or a subquery with aggregation to avoid correlated subqueries.

issues.title: Lack of comments
issues.problem: The query lacks comments explaining the logic, especially around the failure rate calculation.
issues.fix: Add comments explaining the logic of the query, especially around the failure rate calculation.

review.corrected_sql:
WITH daily_transactions AS (
  SELECT transaction_date, COUNT(*) as total_count, SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'FAILED' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as failed_count
  FROM fact_transactions
  GROUP BY transaction_date
),
total_transactions AS (
  SELECT SUM(total_count) as total_count
  FROM daily_transactions
)
SELECT transaction_date, failed_count, total_count, (failed_count * 100.0 / total_count) as failure_rate
FROM daily_transactions, total_transactions
ORDER BY transaction_date;
review.summary: The query had a critical correctness issue with the failure rate calculation, a performance issue with a correlated subquery, and a readability issue with lack of comments.
